answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock collateral in a time-locked escrow before it may transact, like a quartz deposit held in a harbor vault: the stake is released only after months of honest behavior, and any proven fraud slashes it. A Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits, while one honest agent needs just one. The escrow acts as a beacon of trustworthiness — cheap to maintain for real participants, ruinously expensive to fake at scale.
